title: RAID5 degraded-mode write limits
content: On a DS920+ volume using RAID5, a degraded array can stay mounted for read access. Continued writes increase the chance of a second-disk failure and unrecoverable data loss. Do not format the volume, rebuild onto the degraded set, or run a repair utility until a healthy replacement disk is installed and the array returns to normal.

title: RAID6 rebuild after a single disk failure
content: A DS1821+ RAID6 storage pool can survive one disk failure and start a rebuild after a replacement disk is inserted. Rebuild time depends on pool size and load. RAID6 is not RAID5: a RAID6 pool should not be treated as if a second failure is immediately fatal, but heavy write load during rebuild should still be reduced.

title: S.M.A.R.T. critical attributes
content: When DSM reports a S.M.A.R.T. warning, treat reallocated sectors, pending sectors, and uncorrectable errors as a replace-the-disk signal. Back up critical shares first. Clearing S.M.A.R.T. history or ignoring the alert does not repair the drive. After replacement, wait for the storage pool to return to healthy before restoring write-heavy jobs.

title: SMB share permission checks
content: If Windows clients cannot open an SMB share, confirm the shared folder permission, the user group, and that SMB service is enabled. A successful DSM login does not guarantee SMB access. Do not reset all ACL entries to Full Control unless the administrator explicitly asks for a permission rebuild and understands inherited permissions will change.

title: DS220+ offline network checks
content: A DS220+ that disappears from the LAN is usually a local network or power issue, not a storage-pool failure. Check the Ethernet link lights, DHCP lease, and whether the unit responds to Find.synology.com on the same subnet. Do not initialize the device or create a new pool while diagnosing an offline DS220+.

title: Crashed storage pool safety
content: If a storage pool shows Crashed, stop writes immediately. Do not format disks, create a new pool on the same drives, or run an online repair that overwrites metadata. Collect the pool status screenshot, DSM version, and drive order. Data recovery options depend on whether the array metadata is still intact.

title: DSM error 13 during folder access
content: DSM error 13 while opening a shared folder usually means the account lacks privilege or the shared folder is unmounted. Confirm the user is in the correct group and that the volume is healthy. Error 13 is not a disk SMART failure and is not a reason to recreate the storage pool.

title: Snapshot Replication file restore
content: Snapshot Replication can restore individual files or a whole shared folder to a previous recovery point. Restoring a snapshot does not replace a degraded RAID rebuild. Ask for the snapshot time, the shared folder name, and whether the customer needs a single file or a full folder rollback.

title: DSM 7.2 update precautions
content: Before a DSM 7.2 update, confirm a recent Hyper Backup or snapshot exists and that no RAID rebuild is running. Updating DSM does not repair a degraded RAID5 array. If the customer only wants a feature from 7.2, check the current version first instead of pushing an immediate upgrade.

title: Hybrid Share sync conflicts
content: Hybrid Share keeps a cloud-backed folder cached on the NAS. Sync conflicts appear when the same file changed both locally and in C2 Storage. Conflict copies should be compared; do not delete the cloud copy to 'force sync' unless the customer confirms the local version is authoritative.

title: Approved reply tone for RAID5 degrade
content: Approved reply pattern: thank the customer, state that the DS920+ RAID5 volume is degraded, ask them to stop heavy writes, and request the pool screenshot plus the replacement disk model. Do not give step-by-step format or initialize commands. Offer to stay on the case until the array returns to healthy.

title: Approved reply for SMB access denied
content: Approved reply pattern for SMB access denied: ask which Windows user is connecting, whether other users can open the share, and attach the shared folder permission screenshot. Suggest checking SMB service and user group first. Do not tell the customer to turn off firewalls as the first step.

title: Approved reply for S.M.A.R.T. replacement
content: Approved reply pattern for a S.M.A.R.T. warning: treat it as a hardware replacement event, ask for a backup confirmation, and collect the drive bay number. Keep the tone calm and do not tell the customer to run a long surface scan overnight as a fix.

title: Approved reply when model is missing
content: Approved reply pattern when the customer omitted the NAS model and DSM version: do not guess DS920+ versus DS220+. Ask for Control Panel > Info Center screenshots and the exact error text before giving any configuration steps.

title: Approved reply that forbids format advice
content: Approved reply pattern for data-loss risk: explicitly say we will not provide format, initialize, or recreate-pool steps. Ask the customer to keep the disks in the current order and send the storage manager screenshot. Mention that a wrong rebuild can destroy recoverable data.

title: Approved reply for DS220+ reboot loop
content: Approved reply pattern for a DS220+ that reboots every few minutes: ask whether the power adapter is original, whether both drive LEDs blink, and whether the unit beeps. This is a device-health reply, not a RAID5 rebuild guide.

title: Approved reply for VIP site outage
content: Approved reply pattern for a VIP customer whose office NAS is offline: acknowledge business impact in the first sentence, give the ticket a high-priority tone, and request network plus device status together. Do not start with generic product-feature education.
